Openings: 1
Job Type: Contract
Duration: 1 Year
Rate: $90–$103/hour W2 + benefits
Hours: 40 hours/week (9 AM–5 PM; no timezone preference)
Project: Nuclear
Interview Process: Virtual, 1 round

The Nuclear Engineer IV will support nuclear plant operations, human factors engineering, plant control requirements, procedures, testing, and engineering documentation. This role requires strong knowledge of nuclear regulatory processes and experience as a Reactor Operator.

Responsibilities

Apply knowledge of nuclear plant operations and nuclear regulatory processes.
Support the human factors engineering process and analyze requirements for plant control.
Review, test, and validate human-system interfaces using a simulator and plant operating, surveillance, and emergency procedures.
Incorporate design requirements into analyses and design documents.
Support the development of normal, abnormal, and emergency operating procedures, alarm response procedures, surveillance procedures, and operator training programs.
Provide plant operation input to the Reliability, Availability, and Maintainability (RAM) program.
Develop proceed/hold acceptance criteria and prerequisites for pre-operational, startup, and selected construction tests.
Support GEH quality requirements, including participation in design reviews and initiation and response to Corrective Actions.
Deliver high-quality engineering documentation on time and in accordance with contract requirements, business procedures, and regulatory agency guidelines.

Qualifications

5 years of experience as a Reactor Operator.
Reactor Operator (RO) license.
Bachelor’s degree in a technical field.

Additional Desired Characteristics

M.S. degree in Engineering or an HFE-related discipline, or equivalent.
Senior Reactor Operator (SRO) certification at a commercial nuclear facility.
Operating or outage experience in positions requiring SRO or RO certification or licensure.
Documented experience delivering high-quality procedures for mission-critical facilities.
Nuclear plant emergency procedure experience.
Experience with procedure writing, training, or surveillance test execution.
Experience with NRC and INPO Operator Training Guidelines.
Experience with NRC Regulatory Guide 0711 or 0711 site implementation and reviews.
Strong oral and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and concisely.
Solid technical writing skills focused on requirements, design, and description documents.
Clear and demonstrated understanding of the nuclear industry.
PPA Procedure Writer’s Certification.
